title: 2021 Fall AMC 12A Problem 8
statement: Let \(M\) be the least common multiple of all the integers \(10\) through \(30,\) inclusive. Let \(N\) be the least common multiple of \(M,\) \(32,\) \(33,\) \(34,\) \(35,\) \(36,\) \(37,\) \(38,\) \(39,\) and \(40.\) What is the value of \(\dfrac{N}{M}?\)

solutions.text:
\(M = \operatorname{lcm}(10, \ldots, 30)\) contains \(2^4\) (from \(16\)), \(3^3\) (from \(27\)), \(5^2\) (from \(25\)), \(7,\) and every prime up to \(29.\)

Among \(32, \ldots, 40,\) the only new contributions are \(32 = 2^5,\) which raises the power of \(2\) from \(2^4\) to \(2^5,\) and the new prime \(37.\) Everything else factors into primes and powers already in \(M.\)

Therefore \(\dfrac{N}{M} = 2 \cdot 37 = 74.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: \(M\) already contains \(2^4, 3^3, 5^2, 7,\) and all primes up to \(29;\) check what \(32\)–\(40\) add
\(32 = 2^5\) raises the power of \(2,\) and \(37\) is a new prime; nothing else is new
